sections.h2: What should a Voorhees homeowner know before selling fast?
sections.html:
A fast sale in Voorhees comes down to three things: whether the township will sign off on the house, how much the state takes at closing, and how quickly a buyer can fund. Voorhees Township is a Camden County suburb of Philadelphia, with a mix of detached houses, townhouses and apartments.

The paths are a traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, or an offer from a buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands. Each path hits the same township and state steps. What changes is how long you carry the house and whether you pay for repairs first.

sections.h2: Where is Voorhees and what shapes its housing market?
sections.html:
Voorhees covers 11.47 square miles of land in western Camden County and was incorporated in 1899 out of Waterford Township. Its population climbed from 1,450 in 1940 to 12,919 in 1980 and 24,559 in 1990, so much of the housing stock went up in those decades. The 2020 census counted 31,069 residents, and the Census Bureau estimates 31,571 for July 1, 2025.

The township borders Cherry Hill, Gibbsboro, Berlin Township, Lindenwold, Somerdale and Lawnside in Camden County, plus Evesham Township in Burlington County. Echelon, the census-designated place in the western part of town, held 11,896 people in 2020. Older names such as Kresson, Kirkwood, Glendale and Osage still show up in addresses and school names.

  • Route 73 (Berlin-Kresson Road) is the only major highway that runs through Voorhees.
  • Interstate 295 and Route 70 reach Philadelphia by way of Cherry Hill, and Exit 32 of I-295 is partly signed for Voorhees.
  • The Ashland station of the PATCO Speedline sits inside the township, and NJ Transit runs the 403 bus to Philadelphia.

Virtua Voorhees Hospital on Route 73 opened in May 2011 on a 40-acre site. The township offices sit at Voorhees Town Center, the former Echelon Mall. New Jersey American Water, the state's largest water utility, was long headquartered here, and the Flyers Training Center draws professional hockey players to the area.

Only 62.0% of homes are owner-occupied, which is low for a New Jersey suburb and points to a sizable stock of condominiums, townhouses and rentals next to the detached houses. If you own a townhouse or condo, ask your association what documents it issues for a sale.

Voorhees Township Public Schools teach pre-kindergarten through eighth grade. The district listed five schools in the 2019-20 school year: Hamilton, Kresson, Osage and Signal Hill elementary schools, and Voorhees Middle School with 1,018 students. High school students attend Eastern Camden County Regional High School, which the township shares with Berlin Borough and Gibbsboro.

Edward T. Hamilton Elementary was named a National Blue Ribbon School in 2003-2004. The Camden County Library's largest branch, the M. Allan Vogelson Regional Branch, is in Voorhees. Buyers with children often ask which elementary zone a street falls in, so have the address ready when you talk to prospects.

sections.h2: What does the township require before a Voorhees house changes hands?
sections.html:
Voorhees runs its resale approval through the township construction office, which handles certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy. Ask that office whether your sale needs a resale certificate, what inspection comes with it, and how long the certificate stays valid before closing.

Unpermitted work is the usual snag. A finished basement, a deck or a converted garage built without a permit can hold up the certificate until the owner closes the permit or removes the work. Pull your permit history early and ask about open items before a contract is signed.

  • State rule for one- and two-family homes: smoke alarms with 10-year sealed batteries must be in place before a sale or change of occupancy (N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19).
  • The state rule does not apply to hardwired or low-voltage alarm systems or to carbon monoxide alarms.
  • Ask the construction office for the current checklist, inspection fee and scheduling window.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when you sell in Voorhees?
sections.html:
The seller pays New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. For a sale over $350,000, the state schedule lists $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000 and $4.80 per $500 for consideration between $200,000 and $550,000. The Census median home value in Voorhees is $429,700, so a typical sale lands in the bands between $200,000 and $550,000. A buyer pays the extra 1% fee only when the price tops $1 million.

Every seller also signs a GIT/REP form for the deed. A New Jersey resident files GIT/REP-3 and owes no estimated income tax at closing, while a seller who has moved out of state may owe 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain in advance. Gain on a principal residence can be partly excluded under federal rules if you owned and lived in the home for two of the last five years.

The county clerk records the deed, and the clerk can reject paperwork that is incomplete. Your closing attorney or title company normally files the RTF-1 affidavit and GIT/REP form together so the deed is accepted the first time.

sections.h2: How do property tax assessments and appeals work in Voorhees?
sections.html:
Camden County is not on the alternative calendar, so an appeal of a Voorhees assessment is due to the Camden County Board of Taxation by April 1, or May 1 in a year with a municipal revaluation. The board is at 509 Lakeland Road, Blackwood, and its phone is 856-225-5238. Owners of property assessed above $1,000,000 may file with the Tax Court directly.

To win, you must show the assessment is out of line with market value, usually with sales of similar nearby homes. A seller who is about to close rarely gains from an appeal, but a buyer or an heir who keeps the house might. State relief for owners of a principal residence includes the Homestead Benefit and the Senior Freeze, and the township handles local deductions for seniors, disabled owners and veterans. Ask the Voorhees tax assessor which deductions are on your account.

sections.h2: What are your options for a quick sale in Voorhees?
sections.html:
The right route depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close.

  • List with an agent: the widest exposure, but showings, repairs, the resale certificate and a lender's timeline add weeks.
  • Sell it yourself: saves the commission, though you handle pricing, contracts and the township paperwork.
  • Take a cash offer: no mortgage underwriting and no appraisal, and a buyer who accepts the house as-is can often close in a few weeks.

For inherited houses, rentals with tenants, or homes with deferred repairs, a cash sale removes the largest delays. Compare the net after fees on each path, not just the headline price.

faqs.q: How fast can I sell a house in Voorhees, NJ?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a few weeks, while a listed sale usually takes longer because of showings, a buyer's financing and the township's resale review. Ask the Voorhees construction office how long its inspection takes so you can plan the closing date.

faqs.q: Does Voorhees require a certificate before a sale?
faqs.a: Ask the Voorhees construction office, because it issues the certificates of occupancy and continued occupancy that apply to a change of owner. State law separately requires 10-year sealed-battery smoke alarms in one- and two-family homes before a sale.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee on a Voorhees home sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. Buyers pay an additional 1% only on purchases of $1 million or more, which is above the Census median of $429,700 for Voorhees homes.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a Voorhees property tax assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is April 1 for a Camden County property, or May 1 when the township has done a revaluation. File Form A-1 with the Camden County Board of Taxation in Blackwood, or call 856-225-5238 for help.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Voorhees house with open permits or code problems?
faqs.a: Yes, but open permits can delay the township's sign-off on a resale. Ask the construction office to review your permit history, then close the permits or agree with the buyer in writing who will fix the items and by when.
